644	## Edge Cases
645	
646	Every outcome below is the exact kernel behaviour **as the design currently stands**; the items that fill a gap in Section C (formerly marked *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-25)* or *(proposed)*) were **ratified as written on 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), R-1..R-20, Open Question 18**, and carry no marker any more. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* "Result event" means the single CR-5 result record, identified by `result_id`, correlated by the caller's echoed `correlation`, appended to the result buffer when the command reaches its terminal state and delivered at the next flush (P5 or the driver's frame boundary) — never during `submit`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
647	
648	**Submission timing and kernel state**
649	
650	- **If `submit` is called during P2 or P5 of tick T (or any phase P0–P6)**: the intake queue has been frozen since P0, so the command is admitted into the *unfrozen* pending set with `queued_tick = T` and is eligible no earlier than tick T+1 (`apply_tick ≥ T+1`, D.4). No result event yet; it is `QUEUED`. From a P5 `INPUT_SURFACE` handler this is the normal and intended path (a menu confirming a selection). From P2/P3 only `SYSTEM`-origin submits exist (CR-3/CR-9); see "a hook submits a PLAYER command" below.
651	- **If `submit` is called while `SAVING`** (reachable only from inside a block's `snapshot()` or another boundary callback, because `SAVING` is atomic within one boundary service): rejected `NOT_ACCEPTING` at admission, exactly as in `LOADING`; nothing is queued, the result is appended to the buffer and delivered at the next flush, and the `SUBMIT_DURING_SAVING` counter increments and a violation is reported (CR-19(d)) — `snapshot()` is side-effect-free by contract, so a submit from inside it is a defect, not a path. This also removes the contradiction a queued command would create when the save returns to `PAUSED` (a `PAUSED` kernel rejects or only paused-service-dispatches). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the earlier text admitted it with `queued_tick = T` and dispatched it at T+1, and is deleted)*
652	- **If `submit` is called while `LOADING`, `BOOTING`, `FAULTED` or `SHUTTING_DOWN`**: rejected `NOT_ACCEPTING` at admission; `submit` returns nothing and calls nothing back — the result is appended to the result buffer during the call and delivered at the next flush, which runs at every frame boundary in every kernel state (CR-5), so the rejection always has a delivery point and never waits for a tick. Nothing is queued. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
653	- **If `submit` is called while `PAUSED` with a type not flagged `allowed_when_paused`**: rejected `PAUSED` immediately, never queued (CR-16), so resume produces no burst.
654	- **If `submit` is called while `PAUSED` with an `allowed_when_paused` type**: *(Ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), R-4; rationale: Section C admits these commands but no tick runs in `PAUSED`, so CR-16 has no dispatch path)*. Rule: while `PAUSED` the driver runs a **paused service cycle** once per render frame consisting of P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 — **no P0 (T does not increment) and no P3 (no hooks)**. Commands dispatch at the current `T` with their ordinary `(queued_tick, host_order)` key; several commits can therefore occur at the same `T`, each logged with its `host_order` so G3 replay reproduces them in order (the control-plane log is part of the replay input, CR-13). The paused boundary runs on every rendered frame while `PAUSED`; no MVP type sets `allowed_when_paused`, so the cycle is exercised only by test fixtures, and a type may carry the flag only if its `writes_blocks` names `gameplay = false` blocks (CR-6, CR-16). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The alternative (make every paused action a control-plane call or pure presentation and drop `allowed_when_paused`, the paused cycle and `writes_blocks` from CR-16) was **not adopted**: the paused service cycle is kept as a retained seam exercised only by fixtures (R-4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
655	- **If `request_resume` arrives after a long pause**: the driver's accumulator is cleared on the `PAUSED → RUNNING` transition, so `ticks_due = 0` on the first running frame; a pause never produces catch-up ticks. The same clear happens on **every** transition into `RUNNING` (`LOADING → RUNNING`, `SAVING → RUNNING`; CR-1a), so a load or an autosave is never followed by a burst. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
656	- **If a control-plane request (`request_pause`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_shutdown`, binding change) is made at any time** — between ticks from UI code, inside a P3 hook, or inside a P5 handler: the call only records it; it is served at the **next boundary**, which is the P6 of the current or next tick or the driver's per-frame boundary service, whichever comes first (CR-15). A request made inside a P3 hook or a P5 handler of tick `T` is therefore served at `T`'s P6; one made between frames is served at the start of the next driver frame, before any tick of that frame runs; one made between two steps of a catch-up frame is served at the P6 of the tick that just ran (the driver re-reads the state, CR-1a). Requests at one boundary are applied in arrival order; the second may become an invalid `(state, trigger)` pair and is then ignored and reported to diagnostics. `request_shutdown` is accepted from every state except `SHUTTING_DOWN`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
657	
658	**Ordering, coalescing and sequence numbers**
659	
660	- **If two commands target the same actor in one tick**: both dispatch in `ordering_key` order (D.7); the second sees the first's applied effects in its `validate` and `apply` (CR-2). No kernel coalescing unless the type declares it.
661	- **If a second command of a `coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK` type arrives for the same `(type, actor, issuer_peer)` while the first is still in the *unfrozen* pending set**: *(Ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), R-5; rationale: Section C does not say where coalescing happens)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* the earlier one is removed (tombstoned, D.8), becomes `SUPERSEDED` and its result is appended to the result buffer immediately (delivered at the next flush); the new one is admitted with its own fresh `host_order` and `queued_tick`. **Only if the newer command passes every admission term** (D.8): supersession is evaluated inside `admitted` with the victim's slot counted as free, so it never fails `QUEUE_FULL` because of the command it replaces, and a newer command that is itself rejected (`ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, `PAUSED`, `MALFORMED`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `QUEUE_FULL`) supersedes nothing and leaves the valid pending intent in place *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. A coalescing type has exactly one allowed origin (boot check `COALESCE_DUAL_ORIGIN`), so the key needs no `origin` component. The key includes `issuer_peer` because admission precedes the authority check — without it a remote issuer could supersede another seat's intent. A P1 batch therefore never contains two commands of the same coalesce key.
662	- **If the earlier intent is already in the current tick's P1 batch when the newer one arrives**: *frozen* means exactly 'in this tick's P1 batch' and nothing wider. A batch member is not superseded — it applies at T, the newer applies at T+1; the batch is immutable after P1. A command that was in the P0 candidate set but fell into the P1 **overflow** (beyond `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK`) has returned to the unfrozen pending set and **is** supersedable, so a newer same-key intent arriving before the next P0 supersedes it and the next batch never holds two commands of one coalesce key. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
663	- **If a `coalesce = NONE` tap (e.g. `begin_weld`) is queued between two intents of the same key** (`[intent A, tap, intent B]`): A is superseded; the queue becomes `[tap, intent B]` in `host_order`. B keeps its own (newer) `host_order` and never inherits A's position — the kernel never reorders. The tap therefore validates against the movement state *before* B, which is the issuer's actual chronology.
664	- **If a `NONE` type is submitted twice in one inter-tick window**: both are queued and both apply; losing one would lose a tap (CR-4). Idempotence of a double tap is the owner's `validate` (`BUSY`).
665	- **If a `seq` supplied by the test ingress or a remote ingress is less than or equal to the issuer's `last_seq` for its `(issuer_peer, origin)`**: rejected `DUPLICATE_SEQ`; nothing else changes (replays and reorders are both caught by this one rule). The rejection's result shares the original command's `(issuer_peer, origin, seq)` and is told apart by its own `result_id` and its reason (CR-5). A local `INPUT_SURFACE` or hook cannot produce one: the kernel stamps its `seq` from a counter that is always ahead of `last_seq` (CR-4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*
666	- **If a test or remote ingress `seq` skips values (gap)**: *(Ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), R-6; rationale: CR-5 has `DUPLICATE_SEQ` but no gap reason)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* admitted; `last_seq` jumps forward; the gap size is added to a per-issuer diagnostics counter. Gaps are expected under VS-B loss and the kernel never retries, so rejecting them would strand every later command. Locally stamped values are dense by construction and never register a gap, even across commands rejected at admission (the counter advances on every submit). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*
667	- **If an issuer's binding is (re)created (new session, VS-B reconnect)**: that issuer's `last_seq` and its kernel-held `seq` counter reset to 0 (the next stamped value is 1) and its rate window clears; `host_order` never resets within a session. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)* A `LOADING` rebuild of the `PlayerId → {(block_id, entity_id)}` half (CR-7) is not a (re)creation: it resets no `seq`, `last_seq` or rate window *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.
668	- **If a `SYSTEM`-origin command is submitted by a hook or handler**: `issuer_peer = 1` (host), `origin = SYSTEM`, and `seq` is stamped from the kernel-held `SYSTEM` counter exactly as a local `PLAYER` command's is from its own (owners never manage it); its result goes to the command log and the diagnostics counters only — **never to the submitting owner or any subscriber** (CR-5, CR-10) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; the earlier 'delivered to the owner at the next P5' text contradicted 'owners never subscribe'; ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling, R-7)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Seq spaces are per `(issuer_peer, origin)` so a SYSTEM command can never collide with the host player's own `seq`. A hook never receives a `SYSTEM` result, so an owner that needs the outcome reads it from state — e.g. Assembly's `NOT_TAKEN` at `submit_T + PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1` — and obeys the CR-9 owner rule (restart-safe, rejection-tolerant, `has_pending` before resubmitting). `SYSTEM` commands count toward `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY` in their own `(1, SYSTEM)` bucket (the `SYSTEM` issuer of D.8), separate from the host player's. The command log records them like any command, but a replay test injects only `PLAYER` commands and lets the hooks regenerate their `SYSTEM` submissions *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from modular-ship-assembly (K1))*.
669	
670	**Dispatch and apply**
671	
672	- **If a command's `actor` was destroyed earlier in the same tick (by an earlier command or, for a hook-submitted command, by last tick's P3)**: the kernel's authority check consults only the binding table, which is identity data and is not touched by domain destruction, so authority *passes* if the issuer is still bound to the key `(actor_source, actor)` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the owner's `validate` then fails on a missing entity and the result is `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)` (Interaction's `INVALID_TARGET` or equivalent). The kernel never checks entity existence (H1). If the session owner has also unbound the actor (honoured at P6, so earliest next tick), the result is `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED` instead.
673	- **If a type declares `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER` and the command's `actor` is none**: `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`.
674	- **If a type declares `allowed_origins = {SYSTEM}` and a `PLAYER` command arrives for it**: `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` **at admission** — the origin is stamped at ingress and the type is registered, so it is known when `submit` runs (D.8). The P2 re-check stays as defence in depth and is reachable only through a test ingress that bypasses admission. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
675	- **If `validate` passes but a published mutator called inside `apply` would violate another block's invariant** (e.g. a weld whose join query said OK but the Graph's mutator refuses): the mutator reports the violation through the fault channel (`scope.fault(code, detail)` and a non-`OK` status, CR-19) — it does not throw or assert. The kernel checks the status after the mutator returns and after `apply` returns, and: stops evaluating this `apply` (its remaining statements are the owner's to skip by propagating the status); does not reach P4 (nothing is committed, notified, logged as applied or saveable); leaves writes already made by this `apply` in the live blocks (no rollback), unreachable to presentation because P5 never runs; transitions `RUNNING → FAULTED`; buffers `Faulted(code)` for the failing command, `Applied` with `detail.uncommitted = 1` for every command already dispatched in this tick, and `Dropped(FAULTED)` for every undispatched batch command and every pending command (CR-5); records `(T, type, issuer, host_order, block_id, code)` in diagnostics. An `apply` that returns anything but its armed `ctx.complete()` token (aborted by an engine script error, or one that returned `null`/`0`) is the same fault with code `INCOMPLETE`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R3)* The dev build halts with the diagnostic; release returns to the menu; no autosave is written (FAULTED rule). Identical in both `KernelProfile`s. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
676	- **If `validate` calls `ctx.reject(reason)`**: that is the ordinary domain rejection — `Rejected(VALIDATION_FAILED(reason))`, the kernel stays `RUNNING`, and it is **not** `INCOMPLETE` (the function reached `return ctx.complete()`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R3)*
677	- **If `validate` reports a fault, returns without the sentinel, calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()`, or has a side effect**: a reported fault, a missing sentinel or a missing outcome is a defect and moves the kernel to `FAULTED` exactly as an apply fault (the command receives `Faulted(code)`, with `INCOMPLETE` or `NO_OUTCOME`); it is not a rejection. Side effects in `validate` are not detectable at run time by the kernel in release; under `STRICT_DEBUG` the `SIM` hash tripwire (CR-12) detects them, and in all builds they are a lint/test obligation on the owner. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
678	- **If a handler calls a mutator outside a `WriteScope`** (from a notification handler, from presentation, from `validate`): the write is refused in every build, no dirty key is marked, the `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` counter increments and a violation is reported (CR-19); under `STRICT_DEBUG` the injected `violation_handler` also runs. The kernel state does not change — this is not an apply fault because no `apply` is running. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
679	
680	**Hooks**
681	
682	- **If hook `after` lists contain a cycle or reference an unknown `hook_id`**: `BOOTING → FAULTED` with the cycle path (or the unknown ID and its referrer) in diagnostics, in every build (CR-6). No partial order is ever used.
683	- **If two hooks have no `after` relation**: ordered by registration index, then `hook_id` (CR-3); the resolved order is printed by the Debug Overlay and is identical on every boot with the same composition root.
684	- **If hook A declares `after: B` but their `(divisor, offset)` mean they never run in the same tick** (fixture: a hook at `(6, 4)` after Graph `(6, 0)` — not Suit's registration, which is `(6, 2)` and co-runs with `graph.propagate.atmo` `(6, 2)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from suit-and-equipment; amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; and the real registered cross-offset pairs: `horror.step` `(5, 0)` after `attention.step` `(6, 0)`; `graph.propagate.atmo` `(6, 2)` after `.power` `(6, 0)`; `.failure` `(6, 4)` after `.atmo`; `sanity.drift` `(12, 0)` after `graph.propagate.failure` and after `suit.vitals`; every one declares `tolerates_stale: true`): the order is still well-defined on the ticks where both run, and A reads B's state as committed by B's most recent run. *(Ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), R-8)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: boot emits a **warning** (not a failure) listing the pair **only when the `after` edge does not declare `tolerates_stale: true`** (CR-3), because staggering and unequal divisors are legitimate when a reader tolerates up-to-`divisor`-tick-old data and the owner says so; a declared edge boots silently, so the warning is not trained away. If the owner needs same-tick data, offsets must match and the divisors must be equal or one divide the other. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
685	- **If a hook submits a `PLAYER`-origin command**: there is no API path — hooks receive only `submit_system()`, which stamps `SYSTEM` (H6). If a hook nevertheless reaches the local input ingress while the kernel's phase is P2 or P3, the command is rejected `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` at admission in every build and the `HOOK_PLAYER_SUBMIT` counter increments (a violation, CR-19; `STRICT_DEBUG` also runs the violation handler). It is never silently re-stamped `SYSTEM`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
686	- **If two or more hooks share a `(divisor, offset)`**: this is normal (`graph.propagate.power` and Attention at `(6, 0)`; `graph.propagate.atmo` and Suit at `(6, 2)`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; they run in the same tick in resolved order. The only cost is a load spike every `divisor` ticks (D.2 `hooks_running_at`).
687	- **If a hook registers `divisor = 0`, `offset < 0`, or `offset ≥ divisor`**: `BOOTING → FAULTED` naming the hook.
688	- **If P3 exceeds `STEP_BUDGET_MS`**: the tick completes in full; the per-hook timings for that tick are logged with the slowest first (CR-17). Nothing is skipped or deferred.
689	- **If a hook reports a fault, returns without the completion sentinel, or trips a step invariant it checks itself**: `RUNNING → FAULTED` exactly as an apply fault (CR-19): P4 and P5 do not run, commands dispatched in P2 of this tick are `Applied` with `detail.uncommitted = 1`, and the pending queue gets `Dropped(FAULTED)` (there is no faulting *command*, so no `Faulted` result). An engine script error inside a hook can only be caught by the sentinel, never intercepted. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
690	
691	**Time and overload**
692	
693	- **If the catch-up cap `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` is reached on one frame**: `ticks_run = 4`, `lag_ticks` reads `ticks_due − 4` at the end of the loop and, at the default `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS = 0`, is dropped in the same frame (D.5); the counter is exposed to diagnostics. The sim is correct and merely behind. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
694	- **If the cap is reached on consecutive frames** (sustained frame time > 66.7 ms at defaults): the sim runs `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` ticks per frame — slow motion, no spiral, because work per frame is capped. Lag is forgiven at the end of every frame (`LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS = 0`, D.5): all lag is dropped, never fast-forwarded, so the player never sees a repayment run, and since no domain system reads wall time the dropped time is observable only in diagnostics. *(Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), Open Question 19: `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS = 0`.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
695	- **If the kernel leaves `RUNNING` inside a catch-up frame** (a P6 pause, a restore, a fault): the driver re-reads the state after every `step()`, stops stepping, and clears the accumulator; the remaining due ticks are not run later (CR-1a). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
696	- **If the tick source is asked about Godot's physics step**: it is not consulted. The driver runs from `_process` on a `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` node and needs no match with `physics/common/max_physics_steps_per_frame`; a Vertical Slice physics projection reads committed state and never steps the kernel (CR-1a). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; replaces the former physics-callback boot assertion)*
697	- **If the queue holds more than `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` commands at P0**: P1 takes the first 128 by `ordering_key`; the rest remain queued with their keys and are first in line at T+1 (CR-17). The 129th command's `apply_tick` is `queued_tick + 2`.
698	- **If a command reaches P2 with age `T − queued_tick > max_age_ticks`**: rejected `STALE`. At the defaults this cannot happen for a local issuer (ratified, R-3) (D.7 finding); it is the VS-B remote-lateness guard.
699	- **If a coalesced (`LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK`) intent is rejected `STALE`**: the actor's intent block retains the *previously applied* intent — a "stop" that went stale leaves the character moving. Consumer rule carried to the Player Controller GDD: an issuer receiving `STALE` for a coalescing type must resubmit its current value from its result handler (the input adapter's quantised-change filter must be bypassed for one send); the result arrives at the next flush and the resubmit is admitted normally — `submit` never calls back, so the handler cannot recurse. The kernel never retries.
700	- **If a queued command's `max_age` would expire while the kernel is `PAUSED` or `SAVING`**: it cannot — `T` does not advance in either state, so age is frozen with it.
701	
702	**Queue capacity**
703	
704	- **If one issuer's pending count reaches `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY` (256)**: that issuer's next submit is rejected `QUEUE_FULL`; all other issuers are unaffected. Supersession still works for that issuer (it frees a slot before the capacity check).
705	- **If the global pending count reaches `QUEUE_CAPACITY` (1024)**: every issuer's next submit, including the local player's and `SYSTEM` submits from hooks, is rejected `QUEUE_FULL`; the hook receives no result (`SYSTEM` results go to the log only) and must tolerate rejection and read the outcome from state (CR-9 owner rule; path (b) targets may reject anyway). In MVP this is unreachable (`2 issuers × 256 = 512 < 1024`); in VS-B it is reachable (Section G). `SYSTEM_RESERVE` (default 0 at MVP; a VS-B suggestion of 128) is slots only `SYSTEM` may use so remote floods cannot starve the host's own systems; it is a normative term of `admitted` (D.8) mapped to `QUEUE_FULL`, not an option. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
706	- **If a submitted payload fails the CR-4 whitelist or exceeds `MAX_PAYLOAD` (4 KiB)** — an object reference, node path, callable, any non-whitelisted `Variant.Type`, a non-finite float, nesting deeper than `PAYLOAD_MAX_DEPTH` (8, which also catches a self-containing container), mixed dictionary key types, or `var_to_bytes(payload, false).size() > 4096`: rejected `MALFORMED` at admission, in every build. A payload of exactly 4096 serialized bytes is admitted; 4097 is rejected. Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the round-trip test (CR-4) additionally reports a violation for any whitelisted payload that fails to survive serialization. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
707	
708	**Notification**
709	
710	- **If a block's dirty set exceeds `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` (256) in one tick**: `change_keys` collapses to `ALL` for that block only; other blocks deliver their key sets normally. The kernel does not retain the individual keys. Every subscriber must treat `ALL` as "re-read everything you use from this block".
711	- **If a block is written but every write restores the original value**: it is still dirty (the kernel marks writes, not diffs); the subscriber may re-read and find nothing changed.
712	- **If a `PRESENTATION` subscriber attempts a block write from its handler**: writes are disabled in P5 — the mutator refuses the write in every build, increments `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` and reports a violation (`STRICT_DEBUG` also runs the violation handler). The notification batch completes for all other subscribers. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
713	- **If a `PRESENTATION` subscriber attempts to submit**: it has no submit handle — the handle is issued only to `INPUT_SURFACE` subscribers at subscribe time and is bound to the local seat (H4). If a `PRESENTATION` script obtains an `INPUT_SURFACE` handle by reference-passing, the kernel cannot distinguish the call and the control manifest/lint is the enforcement; the kernel-level guarantee is that no handle is ever *issued* to `PRESENTATION`.
714	- **If a subscriber handler aborts on an engine script error**: the engine cannot be intercepted (CR-19). The kernel calls handlers one at a time from its own loop, so the abort ends only that handler — the error is printed, the loop continues and the remaining subscribers still receive the batch; the completion sentinel (the handler did not return its armed `ctx.complete()` token) lets diagnostics record the subscriber ID as `INCOMPLETE`. The tick is already committed, so the sim is unaffected. This is **best-effort isolation plus lint**, not a guarantee: a handler is a presentation defect, never a kernel fault. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
715	- **If sim code (any call during P2 or P3, or any registered owner) requests a `PERCEPTION_OUT` read view**: in every build the read returns an empty view (no data, not null — callers should not crash), increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation naming the caller (`STRICT_DEBUG` also runs the violation handler). The owner's own hooks are included (CR-12). A view obtained legitimately outside tick phases and cached for use inside one is a lint obligation.
716	
717	**Snapshot and restore**
718	
719	- **If `request_snapshot` is issued while `PAUSED`**: `PAUSED → SAVING` at the (idle) boundary; capture runs at the current `T` with no tick; return state is `PAUSED`.
720	- **If `request_snapshot` is issued during a cross-block `apply` or any mid-tick phase**: it is recorded and honoured at this tick's P6, after P4 commit; a snapshot can never observe a half-applied command or a mid-P3 state (CR-18, G6).
721	- **If a block's `snapshot()` reports a fault, returns without the completion token, or delivers non-plain data through `ctx.put` (whitelist walk)**: capture error → `SAVING → FAULTED`; the partial snapshot is discarded and nothing is handed to Save/Load; the existing save file is untouched. The pending queue gets `Dropped(FAULTED)`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
722	- **If a restore payload lacks a registered `persist` block**: `default_state()` is used for that block, a diagnostics note is written, and restore proceeds (CR-8; Save/Load decides whether a missing block is acceptable before calling).
723	- **If a restore payload contains a `block_id` the registry does not know**: the kernel's **pre-check** (run over the whole payload before any `restore()` is called) fails with `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK`; state is fully intact (nothing was touched) and the kernel goes `LOADING → FAULTED` per the transitions table. Save/Load is expected to strip or refuse unknown blocks first, so reaching this is a Save/Load defect.
724	- **If a block's stored `schema_version` is newer than the code's**: the owner reports unsupported (never a silent default) — caught in pre-check if owners declare `supported_versions`, otherwise at that block's `restore()`; either way `LOADING → FAULTED`. State is intact only if caught in pre-check.
725	- **If a block's stored `schema_version` is older and the owner has no migration for it**: same path and outcome as "newer".
726	- **If the snapshot header's `TICK_RATE` differs from the running constant**: *(Ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), R-9; rationale: record `TICK_RATE` in the header)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* pre-check fails `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` → `FAULTED`; migrating every tick-expressed value in every block is impractical, so a save is bound to the tick rate that wrote it.
727	- **If any block's `post_restore()` fails (cross-block ID unresolved, invariant violated)**: `LOADING → FAULTED` with the block and invariant named. Because restore is whole-block replace and all blocks have been replaced by the time `post_restore` runs, **pre-restore state is not intact here** — "where possible" in CR-18 means pre-check failures only. *(Option)*: capture an in-memory snapshot of the live state before a mid-session restore so diagnostics can diff; automatic revert to it is out of scope (would need a second restore pass that could itself fail).
728	- **If `request_restore` is made while `SAVING` is active** (only possible from inside the atomic capture): it is queued and served, in arrival order with any other queued request, at the boundary that follows the capture; the queue is flushed with `Dropped(RELOAD)` at that point. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
729	- **If a restore completes while the pending queue is non-empty**: every pending command has already received `Dropped(RELOAD)` at the `→ LOADING` transition; the first tick after `RUNNING` sees an empty queue.
730	
731	**Authority, classes and identity**
732	
733	- **If an `INPUT_SURFACE` submits with an `actor` its seat's PlayerId does not control**: for `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` types → `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED` at P2; for `actor_binding = NONE` types the kernel does not check `actor` at all and the owner's `validate` decides. The surface can never choose its `issuer_peer` (stamped by the handle — H6), so "submitting as another seat" is unrepresentable.
734	- **If the binding table is changed during a tick**: the change is a control-plane request honoured at P6, so every authority check within one tick sees one consistent table; a command admitted before the change and dispatched after it is checked against the *new* table (authority is checked at P2, not at admission). The `LOADING` rebuild of the `PlayerId → {(block_id, entity_id)}` half (CR-7) is the one exception to the P6 rule: it runs inside the atomic `LOADING` service, before any tick, so no tick's checks can straddle it *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.
735	- **If two binding sources deliver the same entity number (Body `(1, 1)` and Emitter `(1, 1)`)**: two keys, `(body.state, 1)` and `(emitter.state, 1)`. There is no conflict, and each `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` type resolves only against its own `actor_source`. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
736	- **If a `PlayerId` is unbound from an entity while that entity has pending `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` commands**: those commands reach P2 and are rejected `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`; they are not dropped early.
737	- **If a peer is bound to a PlayerId that already has persistent `PER_PLAYER` blocks**: nothing in the kernel changes — persistent state is keyed by PlayerId, never peer_id (Vocabulary); the binding only maps the new peer to the existing seat.
738	
739	**Lifecycle, mode and tests**
740	
741	- **If the kernel is `SAVING` when an invariant check (inside a block's `snapshot()`) fails**: see capture error above — `FAULTED`, snapshot discarded, existing save untouched.
742	- **If `FAULTED` is entered while a notification batch is mid-delivery**: impossible — faults originate in P2/P3 (apply, validate, hook), the `PAUSED` service cycle's P2 (`PAUSED → FAULTED`), `P4` (`commit_baseline`) or `SAVING`/`LOADING` (`snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state`, `init_world`, `post_restore`, `binding_source` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*); P5 handlers and `read_view` cannot fault the kernel (a handler's or a view's reported fault or missing sentinel is recorded, CR-19). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
743	- **If `request_shutdown` arrives with queued commands**: every pending command receives `Dropped(SHUTDOWN)` — appended to the result buffer during the `→ SHUTTING_DOWN` transition and delivered by the final flush that teardown runs — then teardown; no further ticks, no snapshot (the FAULTED/shutdown rule: the kernel never autosaves on the way out).
744	- **If the tick counter would overflow**: it cannot — `T`, `seq` and `host_order` are 64-bit (D.14); the boot assertion on width is the only handling.
745	- **If anything attempts to construct or switch the kernel into `MIRROR` mode in MVP**: `BOOTING → FAULTED` with `MODE_UNSUPPORTED`; the `MIRROR` enum value exists so the API is mode-agnostic, but no MIRROR ingress, replication subscriber or constructor is compiled in MVP (H8). An acceptance test asserts that a MIRROR submit is impossible by asserting the construction fails.
746	- **If two kernel instances exist in one process (a test constructing two)**: each has its own registries, queue, clock, binding table and log; a block object registered with a second kernel while bound to a first fails that kernel's boot (`BLOCK_ALREADY_BOUND`) because owners are instance-scoped; an autoload, if one exists, is a thin holder of *one* instance and kernel code never reads it (H10), so the second instance is unaffected by whatever the autoload holds. gdUnit4's orphan-node check (exit 101) is avoided because neither instance is a Node.
747	- **If `TICK_RATE` is changed in code between two play sessions without a save in between**: nothing breaks at the kernel level, but every tick-expressed tuned value in every data file is now wrong by the ratio of the rates; this is why `TICK_RATE` is a set-once constant and why Section G lists every knob it invalidates.

830	## Visual/Audio Requirements
831	
832	None of its own — the kernel renders nothing and plays nothing (H4, CR-11). What it *requires* of visual and audio systems is structural: every presentation element subscribes as `PRESENTATION` (or `INPUT_SURFACE`), reads last-committed state through read views, and interpolates with `tick_alpha` where motion must be smooth. Two consequences for the art bible's rules are worth stating here so they are not rediscovered per system: (1) the art bible's truth-channel / corruptible tag contract (Perception Filter) maps onto the kernel's two consumer channels — truth-channel elements read `SIM` views directly, corruptible elements read the Filter's `PERCEPTION_OUT`-derived channel; (2) the "nothing fails silently" rule of Pillar 1 is served by the kernel only in that every state change produces a notification — *what* is drawn for it is the owning system's Visual/Audio section. No asset-spec flag: there are no assets.

834	## Game Feel
835	
836	Optional for a `Core` system; one target is recorded because it is the kernel's doing. **Input-to-effect latency, empty queue, 60 Hz tick / 60 fps render: typically the first changed frame is drawn within 33.3 ms of the input event and the full committed value within 50 ms, and in the worst case (a 0-tick frame in the path) within 50 ms and 66.7 ms (D.4 `L_first`, `L_full`); the sim confirms within one tick (16.7 ms of simulated time); acknowledgement is immediate.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* A backlog adds one tick per 128 queued commands. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The gameplay-programmer's feel bar: a press should produce a local response in the same frame (tool sound, hand animation start, linear progress bar beginning), with the sim confirming on the next tick; the only visible effect of the command path is a bar that begins a tick later. Movement waits one tick like every command — Body's integration hook reads the current intent in P3 (CR-4) — so the avatar's first response is inside the same bound; only the acknowledgement (a footstep sound, a stance change) is same-frame. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Two anti-targets: no synchronous local fast path for results (it would not survive a remote issuer), and no client-side prediction in MVP (the `seq`/`queued_tick` fields and determinism guarantees are the hooks for it later). Reduced-motion settings never alter the tick (CR-11), so feel and accessibility settings cannot change simulation outcomes. **Aim latency takes no target of its own** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the chest lamp's cone is sim-authoritative, so on a sweep it trails a zero-latency cursor by the D.4 delay (about 2–3 frames); that lag is accepted at the D.4 bounds and the *drawn* cone is not extrapolated (Open Question 23, resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R21), and the spike measures it (KRN-LAT-03) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R21)*.

The tell window: length and the floor (contract part 1).** *Rule.* At TELL entry, `tell_len = rng_int(TELL_DRAW_LO, TELL_DRAW_HI)` (inclusive), drawn with `rng_derive(world_seed, "attention.tell", counter_eff)`, where `counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch` is **the kernel's one derivation for threat draws**, called and never re-derived here (Command & Simulation Layer owns it and `RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE`; Horror calls the same derivation) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)*, then `rng_counter` increments *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(user ruling D16: threat draws re-key per restore epoch)*. Two things stay exact: `rng_counter` is persisted and restored unchanged, and a `tell_len` already drawn is persisted with the block, so a restore taken during a TELL replays that tell's length and beats and cannot reroll it (no reroll oracle). What changes is the key of every draw made **after** a restore. `restore_epoch` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* is Save/Load's persisted u32, held in the per-slot side file `slot_epoch.bin` (each generation header keeps only a read-only copy, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA never change) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14)*: it starts at 0; a death-stub restore advances it by 1, and so does a Continue of any generation other than the newest non-demoted verified `QUIT` generation (after a kill, crash or fallback, in one process or after a fresh start); Save/Load makes each advance durable before it calls `request_restore`. A Continue of that newest `QUIT` generation carries it unchanged, so a Save & Quit then Continue replays the identical tell draws (quit buys no re-roll), while two death restores of one autosave give two new epochs. If the epoch write fails, the restore proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory and Save/Load logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` with `save_status = FAILED`; a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once, an exposure Save/Load lists and owns (R14). The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)`. The only BOOTING exit is the generic 'registries valid and frozen -> LOADING' (L181), which carries no payload or seed. Under KRN-STATE-01 ('an unlisted pair is invalid and writes one invalid-transition entry'), (BOOTING, request_new_game) would be an invalid pair, so KRN-STATE-01 and KRN-STATE-02 cannot both pass as written. There is also no named 'deferred' outcome for requests received during SAVING or LOADING (queued per L170/L198), so the table-driven fixture cannot be generated mechanically.

findings.section: CR-1a driver loop / D.5 / Edge L695 / AC L906
findings.finding: Carried over (G3). The driver 'stops the moment the kernel is no longer RUNNING - a P6 pause, a restore, a fault', but SAVING and LOADING are atomic within one boundary service and the kernel is RUNNING again when the driver re-reads state. Only a pause or fault is observable. An autosave (request_snapshot, honoured at P6) or a death-restore inside tick 2 of a 4-tick catch-up frame therefore leaves the loop running. The accumulator was cleared 'on transition into RUNNING' (the mechanism is unstated), and the loop still computes acc - ticks_run*TICK_UNITS from the cleared value, so acc goes negative and later frames starve, or extra ticks run on the freshly loaded world. AC L906 only tests pause.
findings.fix: Have the boundary service return (or the kernel expose) a monotonically increasing 'entered-RUNNING' serial or flag that the driver compares after every step(); on change stop stepping, set acc = 0 and skip the subtraction. State in D.5 that acc is never negative. Add an AC: autosave honoured in tick 2 of a 4-tick frame runs exactly 2 ticks and leaves acc == 0, and the same for a restore.

findings.finding: Carried over. The AC still calls request_restore(payload, H); CR-15 and Save/Load (L205/223/286) use request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash). As written the AC passes H in the epoch position.
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'WHEN request_restore(payload, e, H) runs ... THEN the first reports {T, computed_hash = H, match = true} ...' and pin the epoch e.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs rows MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK, MAX_PAYLOAD, COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET; D.13; KRN-BND-01
findings.finding: Carried over. Safe ranges still violate the coupled constraints at the defaults. (a) MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK 32-512: at QUEUE_CAPACITY 1024 and 32, ceil(1024/32) = 32 > 30 breaks constraint 1. (b) MAX_PAYLOAD 1-64 KiB cannot boot at 64 KiB under any COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET in range (2048 x ~64 KiB = 128 MiB > 64 MiB); the usable ceiling at the 16 MiB default is about 7.9 KiB. (c) COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET 8-64 MiB: the defaults need about 8.29 MiB (queue 4.195 MiB + log 4.098 MiB), so the bottom of the range fails boot at the defaults. D.13 says the log is '~4.3 MiB' and the knob/KRN-BND-01 say '8.5 MiB'; those are MB-for-MiB mixes (4.3 MB = 4.10 MiB).
findings.fix: Make all three ranges conditional like QUEUE_CAPACITY's ('32..., subject to constraints 1 and 8'). Set COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET's floor to 9 MiB (or 'derived: defaults + 10 %'), restate MAX_PAYLOAD's ceiling as the value that satisfies constraint 8, and use MiB consistently (4.1 / 4.2 / 8.3 MiB).

findings.finding: Carried over. The fold uses the big-operator glyph with no statement that it is ordered concatenation. The byte widths and endianness of T, world_seed, len(block_id), schema_version, len(canonical_bytes) and block_hash(b) inside the fold are not given, and the PACKED element-type byte values (0x09) are not enumerated. state_hash is exchanged with Save/Load (expected_state_hash) and block_hash is stored as block_state_hash, so two implementers can produce different hashes. The worked examples cover only INT, FLOAT and nested arrays, and the section ends without a closing sentence.
findings.fix: State '(+) = ordered byte concatenation', give each fold field its width (u64 LE for T, len and the ids; u32 LE for schema_version; 8 LE bytes for block_hash), enumerate PACKED element-type bytes (e.g. 0x01 Byte, 0x02 Int32, 0x03 Int64, 0x04 Float32, 0x05 Float64, 0x06 String, 0x07 Vector2), and add one PACKED worked example.

findings.section: States and Transitions / CR-18 / KRN-STATE-01, KRN-STATE-02 (L178-198, L910-911)
findings.finding: Carried over from the two previous reviews and still not fixed (G3): the transition table has no BOOTING row for request_new_game or request_restore, yet CR-18 says request_new_game is valid 'at first boot' and KRN-STATE-02 runs it at first boot. The only BOOTING exit is the generic 'registries valid and frozen -> LOADING' (L181), which carries no payload or seed. Under KRN-STATE-01 ('an unlisted pair is invalid and writes one invalid-transition entry'), (BOOTING, request_new_game) would be an invalid pair, so KRN-STATE-01 and KRN-STATE-02 cannot both pass as written. There is also no named 'deferred' outcome for requests received during SAVING or LOADING (queued per L170/L198), so the table-driven fixture cannot be generated mechanically.
findings.fix: Add rows '(BOOTING) request_new_game(world_seed, epoch) / request_restore(payload, epoch) -> LOADING' and say whether the unconditional BOOTING->LOADING row is replaced. Add a DEFERRED outcome class to the trigger vocabulary for requests made in SAVING and LOADING, and list it in KRN-STATE-01's fixture.

findings.section: CR-1a driver loop / D.5 / Edge L695 / AC L906
findings.finding: Carried over (G3). The driver 'stops the moment the kernel is no longer RUNNING - a P6 pause, a restore, a fault', but SAVING and LOADING are atomic within one boundary service and the kernel is RUNNING again when the driver re-reads state. Only a pause or fault is observable. An autosave (request_snapshot, honoured at P6) or a death-restore inside tick 2 of a 4-tick catch-up frame therefore leaves the loop running. The accumulator was cleared 'on transition into RUNNING' (the mechanism is unstated), and the loop still computes acc - ticks_run*TICK_UNITS from the cleared value, so acc goes negative and later frames starve, or extra ticks run on the freshly loaded world. AC L906 only tests pause.
findings.fix: Have the boundary service return (or the kernel expose) a monotonically increasing 'entered-RUNNING' serial or flag that the driver compares after every step(); on change stop stepping, set acc = 0 and skip the subtraction. State in D.5 that acc is never negative. Add an AC: autosave honoured in tick 2 of a 4-tick frame runs exactly 2 ticks and leaves acc == 0, and the same for a restore.

The publisher spells it SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE: Save/Load (9 hits), Attention L196, Horror L257 and the registry. findings.fix: Replace every SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE in CR-15, KRN-EPO-05 and OQ 24 with SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE and delete the alias parenthetical.

findings.section: States and Transitions / CR-18 / KRN-STATE-01, KRN-STATE-02 (L178-198, L910-911)
findings.finding: Carried over from the two previous reviews and still not fixed (G3): the transition table has no BOOTING row for request_new_game or request_restore, yet CR-18 says request_new_game is valid 'at first boot' and KRN-STATE-02 runs it at first boot. The only BOOTING exit is the generic 'registries valid and frozen -> LOADING' (L181), which carries no payload or seed. Under KRN-STATE-01 ('an unlisted pair is invalid and writes one invalid-transition entry'), (BOOTING, request_new_game) would be an invalid pair, so KRN-STATE-01 and KRN-STATE-02 cannot both pass as written. There is also no named 'deferred' outcome for requests received during SAVING or LOADING (queued per L170/L198), so the table-driven fixture cannot be generated mechanically.
findings.fix: Add rows '(BOOTING) request_new_game(world_seed, epoch) / request_restore(payload, epoch) -> LOADING' and say whether the unconditional BOOTING->LOADING row is replaced. Add a DEFERRED outcome class to the trigger vocabulary for requests made in SAVING and LOADING, and list it in KRN-STATE-01's fixture.

findings.section: CR-1a driver loop / D.5 / Edge L695 / AC L906
findings.finding: Carried over (G3). The driver 'stops the moment the kernel is no longer RUNNING - a P6 pause, a restore, a fault', but SAVING and LOADING are atomic within one boundary service and the kernel is RUNNING again when the driver re-reads state. Only a pause or fault is observable. An autosave (request_snapshot, honoured at P6) or a death-restore inside tick 2 of a 4-tick catch-up frame therefore leaves the loop running. The accumulator was cleared 'on transition into RUNNING' (the mechanism is unstated), and the loop still computes acc - ticks_run*TICK_UNITS from the cleared value, so acc goes negative and later frames starve, or extra ticks run on the freshly loaded world. AC L906 only tests pause.
findings.fix: Have the boundary service return (or the kernel expose) a monotonically increasing 'entered-RUNNING' serial or flag that the driver compares after every step(); on change stop stepping, set acc = 0 and skip the subtraction. State in D.5 that acc is never negative. Add an AC: autosave honoured in tick 2 of a 4-tick frame runs exactly 2 ticks and leaves acc == 0, and the same for a restore.

findings.section: CR-15 and Acceptance Criteria KRN-EPO-05; Open Question 24
findings.finding: The kernel names the failure log 'SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE' (CR-15 with 'R14's SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE' as an alias, KRN-EPO-05, OQ 24). The publisher spells it SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE: Save/Load (9 hits), Attention L196, Horror L257 and the registry. G1 says the publisher's spelling wins, and KRN-EPO-05 asserts a log string that Save/Load will not emit, so it fails against the real Save/Load. Carried over from the previous review.
findings.fix: Replace every SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE in CR-15, KRN-EPO-05 and OQ 24 with SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE and delete the alias parenthetical.

findings.section: Cross-GDD: web-map-and-transit.md vs kernel CR-6/CR-7; Open Question 24
findings.finding: CR-6 makes actor_binding mandatory with no silent default and fails boot otherwise. Web Map's PLAYER commands pod_hop, berth and unberth (registry web_commands.player_origin) state no actor_binding or actor_source anywhere: web-map-and-transit.md has zero actor_binding, OWNED_BY_ISSUER or actor_source hits, and only the SYSTEM rows say 'no actor binding'. OQ 24's list of OWNED_BY_ISSUER registrants (Player Controller, Interaction, Suit, Assembly, Emitter) omits Web Map, so the composition root cannot register these types.
findings.fix: In web-map-and-transit.md and the registry web_commands entry, declare actor_binding for the three PLAYER types: NONE if the console subject is the authority, or OWNED_BY_ISSUER with actor_source body.state if the acting avatar must be the issuer's. Add Web Map to OQ 24 and make the choice consistent with Interaction's console verbs.

CR-7 and the FAULTED rows say a source that faults or omits the sentinel takes LOADING -> FAULTED, but a lint built from the CR-19(a) list would never check binding_source's -> void and return ctx.complete() rules. CR-15's request list also omits the session-owner binding change that Edge L656/L734 and AC L933 treat as a P6 request.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs rows MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK, MAX_PAYLOAD, COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET; D.13; KRN-BND-01
findings.finding: Carried over. Safe ranges still violate the coupled constraints at the defaults. (a) MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK 32-512: at QUEUE_CAPACITY 1024 and 32, ceil(1024/32) = 32 > 30 breaks constraint 1. (b) MAX_PAYLOAD 1-64 KiB cannot boot at 64 KiB under any COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET in range (2048 x ~64 KiB = 128 MiB > 64 MiB); the usable ceiling at the 16 MiB default is about 7.9 KiB. (c) COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET 8-64 MiB: the defaults need about 8.29 MiB (queue 4.195 MiB + log 4.098 MiB), so the bottom of the range fails boot at the defaults. D.13 says the log is '~4.3 MiB' and the knob/KRN-BND-01 say '8.5 MiB'; those are MB-for-MiB mixes (4.3 MB = 4.10 MiB).
findings.fix: Make all three ranges conditional like QUEUE_CAPACITY's ('32..., subject to constraints 1 and 8'). Set COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET's floor to 9 MiB (or 'derived: defaults + 10 %'), restate MAX_PAYLOAD's ceiling as the value that satisfies constraint 8, and use MiB consistently (4.1 / 4.2 / 8.3 MiB).

findings.finding: Carried over. The fold uses the big-operator glyph with no statement that it is ordered concatenation. The byte widths and endianness of T, world_seed, len(block_id), schema_version, len(canonical_bytes) and block_hash(b) inside the fold are not given, and the PACKED element-type byte values (0x09) are not enumerated. state_hash is exchanged with Save/Load (expected_state_hash) and block_hash is stored as block_state_hash, so two implementers can produce different hashes. The worked examples cover only INT, FLOAT and nested arrays, and the section ends without a closing sentence.
findings.fix: State '(+) = ordered byte concatenation', give each fold field its width (u64 LE for T, len and the ids; u32 LE for schema_version; 8 LE bytes for block_hash), enumerate PACKED element-type bytes (e.g. 0x01 Byte, 0x02 Int32, 0x03 Int64, 0x04 Float32, 0x05 Float64, 0x06 String, 0x07 Vector2), and add one PACKED worked example.

findings.section: CR-4 seq / D.8 last_seq / Edge L665 / KRN-SEQ-01
findings.finding: Carried over. Edge L665 and D.8 say a local stamp is 'always ahead of last_seq', but the test ingress (KRN-SEQ-01 injects seq = 5) raises last_seq above the kernel's stamp counter; the next local submit would then be stamped 4 and rejected DUPLICATE_SEQ. data.summary: Verdict: APPROVED, no BLOCKING defects. The one prior blocker, the CR-7 binding rebuild keying, is resolved in this file and in the siblings it named. CR-7 half (b) is keyed (source block_id, entity_id); actor_source is declared by every OWNED_BY_ISSUER type in Emitter, Player Controller, Interaction, Suit and Assembly; KRN-BIND-05 and Edge L735 cover the Body/Emitter collision; the registry matches. All 8 sections are present and every Dependencies GDD exists except the undesigned VS-B Co-op Session (R9, not a blocker). The formulas and ACs I recomputed at registry defaults are consistent: D.4 apply_tick, D.5 accumulator examples, D.8 admission and queue ceilings, D.10 goldens and epoch vectors, D.12 SHA-256 H64 pin, ticks_for_seconds, hooks_running_at, the 25-formula count and the KRN-BIND-05 expectations. Fourteen RECOMMENDED items remain, most carried over from earlier passes. Rank them: (1) the BOOTING request_new_game/request_restore table gap, where KRN-STATE-01 and KRN-STATE-02 disagree; (2) the driver's unobservable atomic SAVING/LOADING round trip, so the accumulator can go negative after an autosave in a catch-up frame; (3) the SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE spelling that KRN-EPO-05 asserts and Save/Load never emits; (4) Web Map's PLAYER commands declaring no actor_binding, which fails boot under CR-6; (5) binding_source missing from the CR-19(a) callable list and KRN-CTX-07. The safe ranges for MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK, MAX_PAYLOAD and COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET still break constraints 1 and 8 at or near defaults. State-hash fold widths, the H1 allow-list, OQ 17 (R21), the seven systems-index edges and the stale D.10 horror.tell note are also open. The spike-gated and PLACEHOLDER items (KRN-LAT-03 no pass line, performance ACs pending spike on RM-DESKTOP/RM-DECK) are intentional and not flagged as defects. The review-receipt check shows both the GDD and the registry changed since the last logged review, as expected after the cross-GDD pass."
